summary: Strawberry Mountain site in the Mount St. Helens monument: 1926 cupola cabin by Bill Roe, a 1931 L-4 pole tower removed in the 1950s; metal and cable remain on the summit.

facts.design: Shake-sided cupola cabin built in 1926; replaced in 1931 by a 15-foot pole tower with gable-roofed L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Removed in the 1950s, though sources differ on removal versus destruction; summit has cable, possible buried footings and metal

access.note: Hike from a parking area at a pass inside Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument; a Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park. No source says the summit is closed

visit.trail_note: Hiking distance under 1 mile from the parking area, per WillhiteWeb

events.note: Shake-sided cupola cabin built by Bill Roe
A September 1926 item says Bill Roe lived on the peak and was building the new station
Cupola replaced by a 15-foot pole tower with gable-roofed L-4 cab

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says it was removed in the 1950s, the listing page says destroyed in the 1950s, and Hite says removed in the 1950s. Hite's trailhead sign gives the lookout's span as 1931 to 1967, which does not match the 1950s end date. The story reports both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Removal wording and dates conflict (removed versus destroyed; 1950s versus a 1967 end on a trailhead sign). The story does not pick one. The 1964 entry is a notice that lookouts would be closed, not a record that closure happened. The weebly page also lists an activation from August 31, 1942 to July 1, 1943 under the Seattle Filter Center, with no detail, and it is left out of the story. Brief said Strawberry Lookout Site with elevation 1665.4 m; register gives 1,665 m. Access is set to public from the Mountaineers and Hite route notes. No photo URLs were captured.
